newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ATLETICO AND BARCELONA DRAW 2-2 IN ILL-TEMPERED CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ATLETICO AND BARCELONA DRAW 2-2 IN ILL-TEMPERED CUP TIE.

text.p: Barcelona striker Juan Pizzi proved he can fill the shoes of Brazilian team mate Ronaldo by scoring twice against Atletico Madrid in a bad-tempered Spanish Cup quarter-final, first leg match on Wednesday.
The 2-2 draw was marked by heavy challenges by players of both sides and a particularly nasty incident in which Barcelona's Fernando Couto dug his spikes into Diego Simeone's thigh.
Atletico went ahead after 19 minutes through Simeone. He was on hand to knock in a loose ball after the Barcelona defence failed to clear a long throw.
But shortly afterwards Simeone was left bleeding after jumping for a high ball with Portuguese international Couto, who was lucky to receive only a yellow card for the foul.
Barcelona equalised just before halftime when Luis Figo was brought down by Daniel Prodan and goalkeeper Jose Molina narrowly failed to keep out Pizzi's spot kick.
Pizzi himself bled freely from the nose after a clash of heads 20 minutes into the second half but recovered to head home a cross from Figo just two minutes later.
Kiko Narvaez levelled the scores 15 minutes from time after controlling a ball with his back to Couto and turning superbly to beat goalkeeper Vitor Baia.
Atletico owner Jesus Gil was unusually mild in his comments about the ill-tempered tie.
In Wednesday's other game Betis beat Rayo Vallecano 2-0 but will feel they should have been in a position to take a greater advantage to the second leg.
The first leg ties continue on Thursday with Las Palmas meeting Espanyol and Celta Vigo playing Racing Santander.
